game.title: Prince of Persia
game.engine: Scimitar (the first Scimitar title; later renamed Anvil)
game.build_notes: Written 2026-09-07 against the Steam build on Windows 10, dev PC. PrinceOfPersia_Launcher.exe is PE32/i386 and is wrapped in SteamStub Variant 2.1 — .text is encrypted at rest, so any string or code scan of the shipped file returns a false negative. Everything below marked inferred-static was read from a Steamless v3.1.0.5-unpacked COPY. The game WAS launched and driven on 2026-09-07 with explicit permission. Windowed mode is verified live; input automation is NOT solved.

input.api: DirectInput8 (keyboard + mouse) and XInput (pad). Driven by INJECTION inside GetDeviceState, not by any Windows input API.
api_notes: SOLVED 2026-09-07: this game is driven by writing into the state buffer it asks for, inside IDirectInputDevice8::GetDeviceState, via a d3d9-style dinput8.dll proxy plus a shared-memory block. Harness: staging/prince-of-persia-2008-vr/proxy-dinput8/tools/pop_input.py. Verified live - one held key drove the applied counter to 355 in six seconds, the game's own log flipped from 'keys down 0' to 1, and two injected DOWN taps moved the main-menu highlight exactly two rows.

⚠️ THE CORRECTION THIS ENTRY EXISTS FOR: an early 2026-09-07 reading of 'SendInput does nothing, PostMessage works' was WRONG and is withdrawn. The title screen is an ATTRACT/DEMO REEL on an idle timer; a 60-second no-input control advanced it with nothing sent at all. The apparent PostMessage success was the timer.

Two cheap explanations are eliminated. Focus is genuinely held: GetFocus == GetActiveWindow == the game window, read from the game's own thread under AttachThreadInput. UIPI is not blocking: game and injector are both S-1-16-8192 (Medium), neither elevated.

Remaining hypotheses, with the observation that separates each: (1) the game polls a GAMEPAD on this screen — plug in or emulate a pad and see if the attract screen advances; (2) DirectInput8 with an exclusively-acquired keyboard — proxy dinput8.dll and see whether DirectInput8Create/GetDeviceState is called at all, which is the most informative and costs one rebuild since we already own d3d9.dll; (3) input is ignored during the attract sequence specifically — post keys at ~10 Hz for a full cycle and see whether the transition ever happens off-schedule.
Capture works: BitBlt from the screen DC against the window rect. Do NOT use PrintWindow (UNIVERSAL.md).

bindings.notes: OR semantics: injection never clears a key the human is physically holding.

entry_points.description: The game MUST be started through Steam. Launching PrinceOfPersia_Launcher.exe directly fails: our proxy loads and reads its config, then the process exits after ~0.6 s without ever calling Direct3DCreate9. Steam instead runs Launcher\Launcher.exe -uplay_steam_mode, a Ubisoft config dialog, which then starts the game.

⭐ The Ubisoft launcher dialog IS drivable, even though the game itself is not. It is an ordinary Win32 dialog: EnumChildWindows returns three Buttons — 'Launch the game!', 'Settings', 'Quit' — and BM_CLICK (0x00F5) on the first starts the game. No synthetic input, no pixel matching.
entry_points.route: EnumChildWindows on the Launcher process main window, then SendMessage(hwndButton, BM_CLICK, 0, 0)
entry_points.notes: 'Settings' is unexplored and is where the launcher writes the HKCU ....0\Launcher registry values; worth a look for display options.

dispatch_notes: This game has NO in-game console proven to exist. What it does have is a large COMMAND-LINE switch table, read out of the unpacked exe on 2026-09-07: 97 switch-shaped names in one contiguous .rdata pool around file offset 0x929640.

⚠️ A switch name existing in the binary is a LEAD, NOT EVIDENCE the switch does anything. Retail builds routinely keep the strings for stripped features — this estate has already been burned by exactly that on Enslaved, where shipped console bindings drive a console that is not there. None of these has been run.
The presence of 'noconsole' implies a console exists to be suppressed, which is why the board carries a [FLAT] row to launch WITHOUT /noconsole and look for one. That row is still unrun.

Switch syntax is '/name' and '/name:value' — established independently in ENGINE-DOSSIER.md section 9 from the exe's own DEFAULT command-line string (e.g. '/world:POP0WORLD', '/mission:pop0_root', '/shadows:off'). That default string is also evidence that a handful of these are genuinely wired, which is a stronger footing than the raw name pool.

absent.notes: There is NO windowed-mode command-line switch. The full switch pool was read from the unpacked exe and holds nothing display-related beyond testvideo/msaa/shadows/postfx/fixedfov/fardist/neardist. A whole-file case-insensitive search for 'window' returns only Win32 API import names, the literal 'Windows', and one non-switch 'window'. Do not go looking for this again.

hazards.title: Windowed mode exists only through our own d3d9 proxy
hazards.detail: The game ships no windowed switch (see commands.absent) and no windowed registry value — HKCU\Software\Ubisoft\Prince of Persia\1.0\Engine carries ScreenResolutionWidth/Height, VerticalSync, Antialiasing, AspectRatioOverride, Shadows, PostEffects and nothing about fullscreen. As of 2026-09-07 the project's d3d9.dll proxy hooks IDirect3D9::CreateDevice (vtable slot 16) and IDirect3DDevice9::Reset (slot 16) and forces Windowed=TRUE, FullScreen_RefreshRateInHz=0, BackBufferFormat=D3DFMT_UNKNOWN, then reframes the game window to a titled 1280x720. Controlled by pop_vr.ini beside the exe; Windowed=0 turns it off with no rebuild, and deleting d3d9.dll reverts everything.
hazards.notes: VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07, n=1 launch. The game requests 1920x1080 fullscreen at refresh 60 (matching the registry exactly, an independent confirmation of that read) and receives a 1280x720 windowed device; CreateDevice returns D3D_OK; the window measures 1286x749 outer with a client area of exactly 1280x720, WS_POPUP clear and WS_CAPTION set. Reset is hooked but no Reset was observed, so alt-tab behaviour is still untested.

hazards.title: Static scans of the shipped exe return false negatives
hazards.detail: PrinceOfPersia_Launcher.exe is SteamStub Variant 2.1: .text entropy 8.00, entry point in a .bind section outside .text. Any string, immediate or code search against the shipped file is scanning ciphertext and CANNOT return a positive. Unpack a COPY with Steamless v3.1.0.5 first; the result should show entry point 0x00B076BD and .text entropy 6.61.

hazards.title: Steam file verification silently reverts data mods
hazards.detail: DataPC.forge is currently a patched archive (CR_Debug_1stPerson's state list rewritten to (309,309,309), deployed 2026-09-07). Steam's 'verify integrity of game files' will replace it without warning, because it no longer matches the manifest. If a data-driven mod stops working for no reason, check this first.

hazards.title: The title screen advances on its own — it will fake an input success
hazards.detail: PRESS ANY KEY runs a demo reel on an idle timer and returns to the title afterwards. A session that presses a key, sees the screen change and concludes the key worked will be wrong. This already happened on 2026-09-07. Always run a no-input control of at least 60 seconds before crediting any input route.

hazards.title: The title screen only responds to a GAMEPAD
hazards.detail: PRESS ANY KEY polls no DirectInput at all; plugging in a DualSense with Steam Input advanced it immediately. An xinput1_3 proxy that can fabricate a pad is built (proxy-xinput/) and pinned to the ordinals the exe imports by, but it has NEVER FIRED - the game was not observed calling XInputGetState - so unattended launch-to-gameplay is NOT yet proven.

automation_capabilities.note: Scored after the 2026-09-07 session that built the injector.

menu_to_gameplay.notes: Steam launch and the Ubisoft launcher's 'Launch the game!' button are automated (BM_CLICK, n=2). The main menu is fully drivable by injection. The gap is the TITLE screen, which wants a pad - the virtual pad is built but unproven.

issue_commands.notes: no console proven; the 97 command-line switches are static leads, none run

move_character_and_camera.notes: the keyboard path that drives menus is the same one gameplay uses and is polled at ~200 Hz there, so this is expected to work, but no character or camera motion has actually been driven yet. Mouse injection is host-tested only.

self_close.notes: the process can be killed; a graceful route via the menu's Quit entry is now plausible since the menu is drivable, but has not been done
